prompt_html: Two main types of options contracts are:
A holder of a call contract is obligated to buy stock at a pre-determined price before the contract expires.
The premium for a put contract is set at a fixed price:
An owner of a call option contract may:
choices_html: Sell the option to another buyer during the lifetime of the contract.
Sell stock at the prevailing market price to the contract writer when exercising their right.
Under no circumstances allow the contract to expire worthless.
Avoid paying a premium when exercising their right.

prompt_html: If an option expires worthless at expiry,
choices_html: The premium paid to the holder will be the buyer’s maximum loss.
The premium paid to the owner will be the writer’s maximum loss.
The premium paid to the seller will be the holder’s maximum loss.
The premium received by the buyer will be the writer’s maximum gain.
